records.law: Constitution of Pakistan, 1973 — Article 58(2)(b)
instruments: Constitution (Eighth Amendment) Act, 1985 (Act XVIII of 1985), effective 11 Nov 1985 — inserted clause (b)
Constitution (Thirteenth Amendment) Act, 1997 (Act I of 1997), effective 3 Apr 1997 — omitted clause (b)
Constitution (Seventeenth Amendment) Act, 2003 (Act III of 2003), effective 31 Dec 2003 — revived clause (b)
Constitution (Eighteenth Amendment) Act, 2010 (Act X of 2010), effective 19 Apr 2010 — omitted clause (b)
records.provision_affected: Article 58(2)(b) — presidential dissolution of the National Assembly
records.chain: original (no clause b, 1973) -> inserted (1985) -> omitted (1997) -> revived (2003) -> omitted (2010, current)
records.current_text: President may dissolve the National Assembly in discretion where a vote of no-confidence has been passed against the Prime Minister and no other member is likely to command the majority, as ascertained in a session summoned for the purpose.
records.repeal_or_supersession: clause (b) omitted by the Eighteenth Amendment (current)
records.source: Gazette of Pakistan — Eighth/Thirteenth/Seventeenth/Eighteenth Amendment Acts

records.law: Constitution of Pakistan, 1973 — Article 260(3)
instruments: Constitution (Second Amendment) Act, 1974 (Act XLIX of 1974), effective 17 Sep 1974
records.provision_affected: Article 260(3) — definition of non-Muslim
records.chain: original definition replaced (1974, current)
records.current_text: a person who is not a Muslim and includes a person belonging to the Christian, Hindu, Sikh, Buddhist or Parsi community, a person of the Qadiani group or the Lahori group (who call themselves 'Ahmadis' or by any other name), or a Bahai, and a person belonging to any of the scheduled castes.

records.law: Constitution of Pakistan, 1973 — Eighteenth Amendment (Act X of 2010), effective 19 Apr 2010
instruments: Constitution (Eighteenth Amendment) Act, 2010
records.provision_affected: Articles 1, 25A, 58(2)(b), 175A, Fourth Schedule (Concurrent Legislative List) and related
records.chain: single omnibus amendment (2010, current)
records.current_text: NWFP renamed Khyber Pakhtunkhwa; Article 25A free and compulsory education age 5-16; Concurrent Legislative List abolished; Article 175A judicial appointments via Judicial Commission and Parliamentary Committee; President's discretionary powers reduced.

records.law: Constitution of Pakistan, 1973 — Twenty-fifth Amendment (Act XXXVII of 2018), effective 31 May 2018
instruments: Constitution (Twenty-fifth Amendment) Act, 2018
records.provision_affected: Articles 246, 247 — FATA merger into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
records.chain: FATA separate administered area (pre-2018) -> merged into KP (2018, current)
records.current_text: Former tribal agencies and frontier regions form part of KP; KP jurisdiction extended; phased application of laws.
records.repeal_or_supersession: FATA status of the Tribal Areas removed

records.law: Constitution of Pakistan, 1973 — Twenty-sixth Amendment (Act XXVI of 2024), effective 21 Oct 2024
instruments: Constitution (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 2024
records.provision_affected: Articles 38 (riba), 175/191A framework (constitutional benches), CJP tenure, Supreme Court strength
records.chain: single amendment (2024, current)
records.current_text: Constitutional Benches of the Supreme Court established; CJP tenure fixed at three years with senior-most judge as Chief Justice; State to eliminate riba as early as possible; Supreme Court capped at 34 judges including the Chief Justice.
records.source: Constitution (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 2024, Gazette of Pakistan
records.verification: verified (corpus current only up to the 26th Amendment)

records.law: Pakistan Penal Code, 1860 — Section 295-C
instruments: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1986 (Act III of 1986)
records.provision_affected: inserted new Section 295-C after Section 295-B
records.chain: no prior s.295-C (before 1986) -> inserted (1986, current)
records.current_text: Whoever by words, either spoken or written, or by visible representation or by any imputation, innuendo, or insinuation, directly or indirectly, defiles the sacred name of the Holy Prophet (peace be upon him) shall be punished with death, or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.

records.law: Pakistan Penal Code, 1860 — Section 302(b)
instruments: Criminal Law (Amendment) (Offences in the name or pretext of Honour) Act, 2016
records.provision_affected: inserted Section 302(b) — offence committed in the name or on the pretext of honour
records.chain: no prior honour-specific clause (before 2016) -> inserted (2016, current)
records.current_text: offence committed in the name or on the pretext of honour is Qatl (murder) punishable as provided for Qatl-e-Amd, notwithstanding forgiveness/compounding considerations that were restricted by the same amendment.
records.source: Criminal Law (Amendment) (Offences in the name or pretext of Honour) Act, 2016

records.law: Pakistan Penal Code, 1860 — Sections 336-A, 336-B
instruments: Acid Control and Acid Crime Prevention Act, 2011
records.provision_affected: inserted Sections 336-A (hurt by corrosive substance) and 336-B (punishment)
records.chain: no prior acid-specific offence (before 2011) -> inserted (2011, current)
records.current_text: Whoever causes hurt by corrosive substance shall be punished with imprisonment for life or imprisonment of either description which shall not be less than fourteen years and a minimum fine of one million rupees.
records.source: Acid Control and Acid Crime Prevention Act, 2011

records.law: Pakistan Penal Code, 1860 — Section 489-F
instruments: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2002
records.provision_affected: inserted Section 489-F — dishonour of cheque
records.chain: no prior cheque-dishonour offence in PPC (before 2002) -> inserted (2002, current)
records.current_text: Whoever dishonestly issues a cheque towards repayment of a loan or fulfillment of an obligation which is dishonoured on presentation shall be punishable with imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both (unless he establishes he had made arrangements with his bank to ensure the cheque would be honoured and the bank committed default).

records.law: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 — Sections 22-A, 22-B (Ex-officio Justice of the Peace)
instruments: Code of Criminal Procedure (Amendment) Ordinance/Act 2002 (sections 22-A, 22-B inserted)
records.provision_affected: sections 22-A (reporting of complaints to JP), 22-B (powers of JP to issue directions)
records.chain: no prior JP mechanism (before 2002) -> inserted (2002, current)
records.current_text: complaints may be made to a Justice of the Peace; the JP may issue directions to the police for registration of cases; aggrieved persons may approach the Sessions Judge against JP orders.

records.law: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 — Section 497 proviso
instruments: Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2004 (women/minors/incapacitated proviso to s.497)
records.provision_affected: Section 497 first proviso — special bail consideration for women, persons under sixteen, and sick/infirm persons
records.chain: main s.497 bail rule (original) -> proviso added (2004, current)
records.current_text: provided that the court may, in its discretion, release on bail a woman, a person under sixteen years of age, or a sick or infirm person accused of a non-bailable offence, even where the main rule would not allow it.

records.chain: Evidence Act 1872 (original) -> QSO 1984 (current, as amended); s.164 recording safeguards retained
records.current_text: confessions to magistrates recorded with the statutory warnings and safeguards under s.164 CrPC; admissibility governed by Articles of the QSO 1984.
records.repeal_or_supersession: Evidence Act, 1872 repealed/replaced by Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984
